↳ Posted by Ampocarbuile on October 27th, 2021.

Bonaparte’s Grand March

This march is called The Grand March by Mícheál Ó Súilleabhain on his LP, Cry of the Mountain (CEF 079 on Gael-Linn). That track is magnificently stately, and rousing, with musicians to match. A setting is given in O’Neill’s “Waifs and Strays of Gaelic Melody” #74, as Bonaparte’s Grand March.

↳ Posted by brailsford on October 27th, 2021.

Napolean’s, X:2

This setting of this fine march is from the Power Manuscript from Kilmore in County Wexford, where it is titled ‘The Grand Cossack March’. I believe it’s to be found in Goodman under the same name. The tune is notated in the earlier part of the Power manuscript which would seem to be mid 19th century. The tune was definitely played in the older local Wexford fiddler’s repertoire, I remember Gerry Forde playing it and even suggesting it as a possible march for playing with the old Wexford ceili band for the fleadh ceili band competitions-but it was always rejected as being ‘too foreign’ sounding. I think this melody may have been used in the soundtrack of the movie ‘Waterloo’, I have a vague memory of that.

↳ Posted by John E Roche on April 29th, 2023.

Bonaparte’s Grand

I transcribed this catchy march from The Shandrum Céilí Band’s album “The Boss Murphy Musical Legacy”. They first play it in G major, then one fifth higher in D major. Since the tune in G major doesn’t fit all trad instruments, I’m leaving here the setting for D major.

If anyone needs a written transposition to another key, they can use online tools for it (Michael Eskin’s ABC transcription tools).

Re: Napoleon’s Grand

English band The Home Service do a stirring rendtiion of this on their latest album. Their brass section helps link to the obvious military origins of the tune. I am not surprised a ceili band found it ‘too foreign sounding’ as it sounds Anglo-French. There were many such ‘foreign sounding’ tunes in Irish musicians’ repertoires in the 19th century before the ITM police got to work to weed them out. The Greig manuscript collection (Leitrim 1880s) contains many military marches similar to this one, which may have come to Ireland via British army military bands.
